name: DEEPTRACE — Downtown Atlanta (illustrative digital twin)
description: Six interdependent infrastructure systems for downtown Atlanta. Street alignments and landmark positions are ESTIMATED; every utility asset, connection and capacity is SIMULATED for demonstration and does not describe the real grid.

region.name: Downtown Atlanta
region.description: Downtown Atlanta focus district: Five Points, Fairlie-Poplar, Centennial Olympic Park / GWCC, Peachtree Center, Civic Center, the State Capitol and Georgia State, Grady and Sweet Auburn, bounded by North Ave, Boulevard, I-20 and Northside Dr. Street alignments and landmark positions are approximate (ESTIMATED); all utility assets and topology are illustrative (SIMULATED). ground_elevation_m is an approximate ellipsoid height (~320 m above sea level minus ~30 m geoid separation).

assumptions: Every utility asset (substations, feeders, vaults, switches, mains, valves, pumps, tanks, fibre, hubs, cell sites, duct banks) and every cross-system dependency is SIMULATED for illustration; none describes the real Georgia Power, Atlanta Department of Watershed Management, carrier or MARTA systems.
Street centrelines are authored approximations (ESTIMATED, typically within tens of metres); landmark positions are approximate public knowledge (ESTIMATED), not surveyed.
Utility routes follow the street graph (shortest path over surface streets) with a fixed lateral offset per system; burial depths are typical values, not surveyed.

Power: 115 kV bulk supply points feed distribution substations over underground cables; each substation feeds radial 12.47 kV feeders (head switch, then network transformer vaults). Normally-open tie switches join feeders of different substations and are rated below full feeder load, so restoration can be partial.
Tie switches are operated remotely over a SCADA control link; if that link is down, a crew closes them manually after properties.manual_switch_hours.

Substation load = rating x properties.load_factor (55-70%); vault loads are split deterministically from stable hashes; population_served is about 1,000 people per MW of load (modelled daytime population).

Water: two transmission-main entries feed a looped low-pressure grid with isolation valves; a booster pump (needs grid power) feeds the high-pressure zone, backed by an elevated tank; normally-closed boundary valves separate the zones and are treated as closed unless opened.

Telecom: dual cores (the 56 Marietta St carrier hotel, whose modelled links are simulated, and a simulated east data centre), west and east fibre rings, a single-homed spur and a mix of single- and dual-homed cell sites; properties.backup_hours is battery/generator autonomy.

Transport: most surface intersections are signalised and need grid power (a few primary-street signals have short UPS backup); one-way flags are recorded in properties.oneway but road edges are modelled as undirected; MARTA traction and station power is modelled as drawn from the nearest network vault.

Facilities: occupancy, backup-generator hours and water-storage hours are modelled assumptions, not published figures. Grady Memorial Hospital is modelled with two power feeds from different substations.
Shared corridors: a feeder, tie or fibre route that runs at least 60 m inside a duct bank or utility tunnel is recorded as hosted (corridor_id); a strike on the corridor fails every hosted edge.
Dependency edges run provider -> consumer (directed); their straight-line geometry is for display only.
Units: power MW, water L/s, telecom Gbps, roads vehicles/hour, rail riders/hour.
Generated deterministically (no randomness); generated_at is fixed so output is byte-stable.
